The search for ""henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex" OR "rtex" "lualatex" "RTEX_TEXLIVE_BIN"" returned the following summary:
**Realtime TeX (`rtex`)** is a tool/library developed by Henry Xiao Yang[1][2] (following Clemens Lode’s TUG 2026 presentation on *Real-Time LuaTeX: Recompiling Large Documents in 1 ms*)[3] that enables ultra-fast, live-updating previews for LaTeX documents as you type[4].

### How it works:
* **Paragraph-level re-typesetting:** Instead of recompiling the entire document on every keystroke, it keeps an unmodified `lualatex` process running in the background (with your preamble pre-loaded) and re-typesets only the specific paragraph you are currently editing in about ~1 millisecond[4][3][2].
* **Background full compile:** Global elements like page breaks, floats, table of contents, and bibliographies are handled by a simultaneous background compilation[4][3].
* **Exact output:** The output matches standard LuaLaTeX output precisely down to 1/65536 pt, and exported PDFs are completely identical to a normal build[3].

### The Role of `RTEX_TEXLIVE_BIN`:
`rtex` requires a working installation of **TeX Live** (or MacTeX) that includes `lualatex`[1][5]. 

While the tool provides scripts to download a minimal built-in TeX Live environment[6][7], if you already have an existing TeX Live or MacTeX distribution installed on your system, you can point `rtex` to it by setting the environment variable **`RTEX_TEXLIVE_BIN`** to your TeX Live binary directory (e.g., where binaries like `lualatex` reside)[1].

### Getting Started:
* **VS Code Extension:** The easiest way to use it is via the *Real-Time TeX Live Preview* extension for VS Code, which manages `rtex` and handles dependencies automatically[8].
* **Source / CLI:** You can clone the GitHub repository (`HenryXiaoYang/realtime-tex`), configure `RTEX_TEXLIVE_BIN` if you aren't using the provided installer script, build it using Rust (`cargo build --release`), and run sessions via CLI commands like `rtex serve`[1][7][5].

To set up and install **HenryXiaoYang’s Realtime TeX (`rtex`)** on **Windows**, you can use the automated VS Code extension method (recommended) or set it up manually[1].

---

### Method 1: Using the VS Code Extension (Recommended & Easiest)

The easiest way to get `rtex` running on Windows is through the official VS Code extension (`Realtime TeX`), which automates the engine and dependency installation[2].

1. **Prerequisites:**
   * Make sure you have **VS Code** (or VSCodium/Cursor) installed[1].
   * You need a TeX distribution that includes **LuaLaTeX** (like TeX Live)[1]. If you don't have one, the extension can help install a minimal TeX Live version on first use[1].

2. **Install the Extension:**
   * Open VS Code, go to the **Extensions** view (`Ctrl+Shift+X`)[1], and search for **"Realtime TeX"** (published by `HenryXiaoYang`)[3].
   * Click **Install** (or find it on the Open VSX Registry if using VSCodium/Cursor)[1].

3. **Initialize the Project:**
   * Open a folder containing your LaTeX project in VS Code[1].
   * Open any `.tex` file[1].
   * Click the **preview icon** in the editor title bar, or press **`Ctrl+Alt+V`**[1].

4. **Follow the On-Screen Setup Prompts:**
   * **Missing `rtex` engine:** The preview will prompt you that `rtex` is missing. Click **Install rtex**. The extension will automatically download the prebuilt Windows binary (`rtex-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip`) and verify its SHA-256 checksum[1][4].
   * **Missing LuaLaTeX:** If LuaLaTeX isn't detected, you can point the extension to your existing TeX Live `bin` folder or let it install a minimal TeX Live environment[1].

5. **Verify Setup:**
   * Open the VS Code Command Palette (`Ctrl+Shift+P`), type and run:
     `Realtime TeX: Check Setup`
   * This diagnostic command checks your environment and provides fixes for any missing components[1].

---

### Method 2: Manual Setup / Building from Source (Advanced)

If you prefer managing the binary manually or want to build `rtex` from source on Windows:

1. **Install Build Tools (If building from source):**
   * Building from source requires **Git for Windows** and the **Visual Studio C++ Build Tools** (typically prompted by `rustup`)[1].
   * Clone the `realtime-tex` repository and build using Cargo:
     ```bash
     cargo build --release
     ```

2. **Using Prebuilt Binaries:**
   * Download the latest Windows release archive (`rtex-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip`) directly from the [HenryXiaoYang/realtime-tex GitHub Releases](https://github.com/HenryXiaoYang/realtime-tex/releases)[4].
   * Extract the archive anywhere on your system[4]. It contains the `rtex` executable, C library/headers, and required TeX support files[4].
   * Run `bin\rtex doctor` via your terminal to ensure it correctly detects your local LuaLaTeX installation and support files[4].

The mention of `build/texlive.env` comes from the project's source build and local setup instructions[3]. 

### How to set up and build `realtime-tex` from source:

1. **Clone the repository:**
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/HenryXiaoYang/realtime-tex && cd realtime-tex
   ```

2. **Install a minimal TeX Live environment locally:**
   The repository includes a script that sets up a minimal TeX Live distribution inside the `build/texlive` directory (takes roughly 15 minutes; on Windows, make sure to run this via Git Bash)[3]:
   ```bash
   scripts/install-texlive.sh
   ```
   *(Note: If you already have an existing TeX Live or MacTeX distribution installed on your system, you can bypass this script and simply point `RTEX_TEXLIVE_BIN` to its binary directory instead[3]).*

3. **Source the environment variables:**
   This loads the necessary paths for the compiler to find your TeX Live installation[3]:
   ```bash
   source build/texlive.env
   ```

4. **Build the project using Cargo (Rust):**
   ```bash
   cargo build --release
   ```

5. **Test the build:**
   You can generate a test book and run an edit check using the built binary[3]:
   ```bash
   target/release/rtex gen-book --pages 10 --out build/fx/book-10
   target/release/rtex edit --project build/fx/book-10 --find "Baseline export" --text " (edited)"
   ```

Alternatively, if you are looking for an out-of-the-box experience without building from source, you can install the **Realtime TeX Live Preview** extension directly from the VS Code Marketplace, which automatically handles prebuilt binaries and minimal TeX Live dependencies for you[1][4].

The **Realtime TeX** extension (`henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex`) for Visual Studio Code provides a live LaTeX preview by keeping a LuaTeX-based engine (`rtex`) running in the background and updating only the paragraph you are actively editing[1].

Below is an overview of the key configuration settings, setup options, and commands available for configuring LuaLaTeX and the extension in VS Code.

---

### Key Extension Settings (`realtimeTex.*`)

You can modify these settings via VS Code's settings UI (`Ctrl+,` or `Cmd+,`) by searching for "Realtime TeX", or directly within your `settings.json`:

* **`realtimeTex.serverPath`** *(Default: `(auto)`)*[2]
  * Path to the `rtex` binary. Leaving it empty tells the extension to use the automatically managed binary (installed via *Install rtex*) or fall back to the one available in your system's `PATH`[3].
* **`realtimeTex.texliveBin`** *(Default: `(PATH)`)*[2]
  * Points to the folder containing your **`lualatex`** executable[3]. If LuaLaTeX isn't automatically detected on your system path, you can explicitly configure this to point to your TeX Live `bin` directory (or let the extension set up a minimal TeX Live environment)[1].
* **`realtimeTex.texDir`** *(Default: `(auto)`)*[2]
  * Points to the `rtex` support files folder (`tex/`). Only needs configuration if you have manually relocated the binary away from its support files[3].
* **`realtimeTex.installFrom`** *(Default: `release`)*[4]
  * Controls whether the *"Install rtex"* helper downloads a prebuilt release binary (`release`) or builds it from source via Rust's cargo (`source`)[3].
* **`realtimeTex.updateCheck`** *(Default: `notify`)*[4]
  * Determines how the extension checks for updates to the `rtex` engine (`notify` alerts you, `auto` updates automatically, and `off` disables checking)[3].

---

### Initial Setup & Troubleshooting

1. **Missing Dependencies/Setup Check:**
   If you run into issues with `lualatex` or the engine, open the VS Code Command Palette (`Ctrl+Shift+P` or `Cmd+Shift+P`) and run:

   This command inspects your environment and offers automated fixes for missing components (such as installing the engine or locating your TeX Live bin path)[1].

2. **Manual Engine Management Commands:**

This combination of terms refers to **`rtex`** (Realtime TeX), a high-performance library and VS Code extension developed by **HenryXiaoYang** (`HenryXiaoYang/realtime-tex` and `HenryXiaoYang/realtime-tex-vsc-plugin`)[1][2]. 

### What is `rtex`?
`rtex` is a real-time LaTeX preview tool designed to eliminate the lag associated with traditional compilation loops[3][4]. Rather than recompiling an entire document on every keystroke (like standard LaTeX workflows or Overleaf do), `rtex` keeps an unmodified **LuaLaTeX** process running in the background with your document preamble pre-loaded[1][5][3]. 

When you edit text, it dynamically re-typesets **only the specific paragraph** you are modifying, delivering updated outputs to your editor in roughly 1 millisecond (~0.5ms to 2ms depending on complexity)[1][3]. Global elements like page breaks, cross-references, bibliographies, and table-of-contents generation are handled seamlessly by a concurrent background compilation pass[5].

### Key Details:
* **Engine:** Uses an unmodified **LuaTeX** instance sourced from a local **TeX Live** installation (or a minimal bundled/auto-installed TeX Live setup)[5][4].
* **Exactness:** Because it relies on actual LuaTeX rather than a simplified markdown-to-pdf parser or subset emulator, the output glyphs, line breaks, and math layout match standard LuaLaTeX builds down to $1/65536\text{ pt}$[5].
* **Ecosystem:** Available as a VS Code extension (`Realtime TeX`) supporting Linux, macOS, and Windows[1][4].

### 1. LuaLaTeX (`lualatex`)
* **Core Engine Integration:** `realtime-tex` relies on an unmodified, warm **LuaLaTeX** (LuaTeX) process from TeX Live[1][4]. 
* **Fast Path vs. Background Full Compile:** Instead of restarting LuaLaTeX from scratch on every keystroke, `rtex` keeps LuaLaTeX running in the background with your preamble already loaded[5]. When you edit text, it re-typesets *only* the specific paragraph you are editing in ~1 ms[1]. A full LuaLaTeX background compile handles global elements like page breaks, floats, table of contents, and bibliographies[4].
* **Setup & Finding LuaLaTeX:** During setup or via extension configurations (`realtimeTex.texliveBin`), the tool looks for your TeX Live bin folder where `lualatex` (or `lualatex.exe` on Windows) resides, or it can help install a minimal TeX Live distribution[2][6].

### 2. Commands (`Command`)
* **Command Palette Integration:** In the VS Code extension (`realtime-tex-vsc-plugin`), all actions are accessible under the **`Realtime TeX:`** prefix inside the Command Palette[7]. 
* **Available Commands Include:**
  * `Open Live Preview to the Side`[7]
  * `Preview This File Only`[7]
  * `Export PDF` (mapped to shortcut `Ctrl+Alt+E`)[8][7]
  * `Recompile Whole Document`[7]
  * `Check Setup` (diagnoses issues with `rtex` or `lualatex` paths and suggests fixes)[2][7]
  * `Install rtex` / `Install rtex (Build from Source)` / `Update rtex Engine`[6][7]
  * `Restart Engine` / `Stop Engine`[7]
  * `Show Log` / `Open Debug Folder`[3][7]

### 3. "Which" / "Where" (Configuration and Path Resolution)
* **Binary Path Resolution (`which` / `PATH`):** 
  * The setting **`realtimeTex.serverPath`** determines where the `rtex` binary is located[3]. Leaving it empty tells the extension to use the version installed via its automatic installer, or fall back to looking up `rtex` on the system environment **`PATH`** (similar to a standard Unix `which` command search)[3].
  * Similarly, **`realtimeTex.texliveBin`** points to the folder **where** `lualatex` is stored on your system (defaulting to searching the system `PATH`)[3].
* **Engine Eligibility / Choice (`which` strategy):** 
  * Under **`realtimeTex.engine.eligibility`**, you can configure *which* parts of your text update live by choosing between `probe` mode (comparing live results against the last full compile) or an `allowlist` mode (permitting only known-safe commands)[3].

When setting up **Realtime TeX** (the `realtime-tex` engine or its VS Code extension), encountering a **"LuaLaTeX was not found"** error means that the tool cannot locate the `lualatex` binary or a valid TeX distribution on your system path[1]. 

To fix this, follow these steps depending on your environment:

### 1. If you already have TeX Live / MacTeX / MiKTeX installed
The engine needs to know where your TeX Live binary folder resides. 
* **Via the VS Code Extension:** When prompted, choose your existing TeX Live `bin` folder manually through the prompt[1]. (For example, path configurations typically look like `/usr/local/texlive/<version>/bin/x86_64-linux` or similar depending on your OS).
* **Via command line (`rtex doctor`):** If you are running `rtex` directly, ensure that your system `PATH` variable includes the directory containing the `lualatex` executable. If you are on macOS using MacTeX, ensure paths like `/Library/TeX/bin` are correctly bound[2].

### 2. If you don't have a TeX distribution installed
Realtime TeX can automatically provision a minimal TeX Live environment for you:
* **Via the VS Code Extension:** Click the option in the setup prompt to **let the extension install a minimal TeX Live**[1]. 
* Alternatively, run the **`Realtime TeX: Check Setup`** command from the VS Code Command Palette (`Ctrl+Shift+P` or `Cmd+Shift+P`), which will check your configuration and offer automated fixes for missing dependencies[1].

### 3. Verify via `rtex doctor`
If you built or unpacked `rtex` manually from a release archive, navigate to its directory in your terminal and run[3]:
```bash
bin/rtex doctor
```
This diagnostic command checks whether `rtex` can properly locate its internal support files as well as your system's `lualatex` installation[3].

# 18. LaTeX Workspace Setup and Realtime TeX Configuration

- **Conversation ID**: `67bebf5f-8513-4f90-a49e-42475fac2f74`
- **Timestamp**: `2026-11-14T11:33:02+06:00`
- **Model**: `Gemini 3.8 Flash`
- **Target File**: [`v2_MM_Lab_Final_Report(PresentationAid).tex`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/Project.MM/FinalReport/v2_MM_Lab_Final_Report(PresentationAid).tex)

---

## Table of Contents
- [1. User Request Summary](#1-user-request-summary)
- [2. Inspected Artifacts & Environment Diagnostics](#2-inspected-artifacts--environment-diagnostics)
- [3. Analysis & Key Insights (Root Cause Investigation)](#3-analysis--key-insights-root-cause-investigation)
  - [3.1 The Architecture of `henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex` and `rtex`](#31-the-architecture-of-henryxiaoyangrealtime-tex-and-rtex)
  - [3.2 Verification via `rtex doctor`](#32-verification-via-rtex-doctor)
  - [3.3 The Missing System Component: LuaLaTeX](#33-the-missing-system-component-lualatex)
- [4. Recommended Solutions & Setup Options](#4-recommended-solutions--setup-options)
  - [Option A: Automated Setup via Realtime TeX Extension (Fastest for `rtex`)](#option-a-automated-setup-via-realtime-tex-extension-fastest-for-rtex)
  - [Option B: System-Wide MiKTeX Installation (Most Robust on Windows)](#option-b-system-wide-miktex-installation-most-robust-on-windows)
  - [Option C: Zero-Config Standalone Tectonic Engine (Fastest PDF Export)](#option-c-zero-config-standalone-tectonic-engine-fastest-pdf-export)
- [5. Verification & Final Outcome](#5-verification--final-outcome)

---

## 1. User Request Summary
The user requested setting up LaTeX rendering in the workspace to edit and preview the project final report located at [`Project.MM/FinalReport/`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/Project.MM/FinalReport). 

When attempting to preview using the VS Code / Antigravity IDE extension `henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex`, the extension crashed with the following error:
```text
Error: lualatex not found on PATH (source build/texlive.env or set RTEX_TEXLIVE_BIN)

Caused by:
    lualatex not found
```

---

## 2. Inspected Artifacts & Environment Diagnostics
1. **Target Report Directory**:
   - [`Project.MM/FinalReport/v2_MM_Lab_Final_Report(PresentationAid).tex`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/Project.MM/FinalReport/v2_MM_Lab_Final_Report(PresentationAid).tex) (complete 206-line IEEEtran conference paper report on the ESP32 micro-NAS & static web hosting node).
   - [`Project.MM/FinalReport/conference_101719.tex`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/Project.MM/FinalReport/conference_101719.tex) (IEEE conference paper template).
   - [`Project.MM/FinalReport/IEEEtran.cls`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/Project.MM/FinalReport/IEEEtran.cls) (local document class).
   - [`Project.MM/FinalReport/fig1.png`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/Project.MM/FinalReport/fig1.png) (figure graphic).
2. **IDE Extension State**:
   - `henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex-0.0.5-universal` installed in `C:\Users\gsmur\.antigravity-ide\extensions\`.
   - The compiled engine `rtex.exe` (v0.0.7) was present in global storage at `C:\Users\gsmur\AppData\Roaming\Antigravity IDE\User\globalStorage\henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex\rtex-release\v0.0.7\bin\rtex.exe`.
3. **Environment Inspection**:
   - Neither `lualatex`, `pdflatex`, `xelatex`, `texlive`, nor `miktex` existed on the system `PATH`.

---

## 3. Analysis & Key Insights (Root Cause Investigation)

### 3.1 The Architecture of `henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex` and `rtex`
`realtime-tex` (`rtex`) provides millisecond-level live LaTeX rendering by keeping a warm, persistent **LuaLaTeX** process alive in the background with the document preamble pre-loaded. When the author edits text, `rtex` does not recompile the entire document; instead, it re-typesets *only* the specific paragraph currently being edited in ~1 millisecond using LuaLaTeX callbacks.

However, **`rtex` is only an orchestration daemon and bridge**—it does not bundle the TeX compiler binaries, macro packages, or fonts itself. It strictly delegates all compilation passes to `lualatex`.

### 3.2 Verification via `rtex doctor`
Directly invoking the bundled diagnostic tool revealed the exact failure point:
```powershell
& "C:\Users\gsmur\AppData\Roaming\Antigravity IDE\User\globalStorage\henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex\rtex-release\v0.0.7\bin\rtex.exe" doctor
```
**Diagnostic Output:**
```text
rtex 0.0.7
support files: C:\Users\gsmur\AppData\Roaming\Antigravity IDE\User\globalStorage\henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex\rtex-release\v0.0.7\share\rtex\tex
lualatex: missing (lualatex not found on PATH (source build/texlive.env or set RTEX_TEXLIVE_BIN))
```

### 3.3 The Missing System Component: LuaLaTeX
Because the host machine lacks a TeX distribution (TeX Live or MiKTeX), `rtex` fails to spawn the compiler process when initiating the live preview panel.

---

## 4. Recommended Solutions & Setup Options

### Option A: Automated Setup via Realtime TeX Extension (Fastest for `rtex`)
The `henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex` extension includes a built-in automated installer for a minimal, self-contained TeX Live environment:
1. In Antigravity IDE / VS Code, open the Command Palette (`Ctrl + Shift + P` or `F1`).
2. Search and select: **`Realtime TeX: Check Setup`**.
3. When the prompt reports missing dependencies, click **Install TeX Live for rtex** (or let the extension download its minimal LuaLaTeX environment).
4. Once completed, reopen [`Project.MM/FinalReport/v2_MM_Lab_Final_Report(PresentationAid).tex`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/Project.MM/FinalReport/v2_MM_Lab_Final_Report(PresentationAid).tex) and click the **Live Preview** icon in the editor toolbar (or press `Ctrl + Alt + V`).

### Option B: System-Wide MiKTeX Installation (Most Robust on Windows)
For full TeX support across all editors, terminal scripts, and automated package management:
1. Open PowerShell / Command Prompt and install MiKTeX via Windows Package Manager:
   ```powershell
   winget install MiKTeX.MiKTeX
   ```
   *(Alternatively, download the installer from [miktex.org/download](https://miktex.org/download)).*
2. After installation, restart the editor or terminal so `lualatex.exe` and `pdflatex.exe` are loaded into `PATH`.
3. MiKTeX automatically downloads missing packages on demand during compilation. `rtex doctor` will report `lualatex: ok`, immediately enabling real-time preview.

### Option C: Zero-Config Standalone Tectonic Engine (Fastest PDF Export)
If the user wants a single, lightweight binary (~25 MB) to directly compile the final paper to PDF without managing TeX engines:
1. Install Tectonic:
   ```powershell
   winget install Tectonic.Tectonic
   ```
2. Build the PDF directly:
   ```powershell
   cd Project.MM\FinalReport
   tectonic "v2_MM_Lab_Final_Report(PresentationAid).tex"
   ```

---

## 5. Verification & Final Outcome
- The exact root cause of the `lualatex not found` error in `henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex` was identified and confirmed using `rtex doctor`.
- Three actionable pathways (in-editor automated setup, full system MiKTeX, and lightweight Tectonic) were formulated and documented to enable seamless LaTeX editing and PDF rendering for [`Project.MM/FinalReport`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/Project.MM/FinalReport).

<#
.SYNOPSIS
    One-Click Automated MiKTeX & LuaLaTeX Installer for Windows.
.DESCRIPTION
    Installs MiKTeX (LuaLaTeX, pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX), configures on-the-fly
    package installation, updates user environment PATH, and verifies
    compatibility with LaTeX editors and VS Code extensions (e.g., realtime-tex, LaTeX Workshop).
.PARAMETER NonInteractive
    Suppresses interactive pauses at script completion.
.PARAMETER Method
    Preferred installation method: "Auto" (default), "Winget", or "DirectDownload".
#>

[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [switch]$NonInteractive,
    [ValidateSet("Auto", "Winget", "DirectDownload")]
    [string]$Method = "Auto"
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

function Write-Step {
    param([string]$Text)
    Write-Host "`n====> $Text" -ForegroundColor Cyan
}

function Write-Success {
    param([string]$Text)
    Write-Host "[OK] $Text" -ForegroundColor Green
}

function Write-Info {
    param([string]$Text)
    Write-Host "[INFO] $Text" -ForegroundColor Gray
}

function Write-Warn {
    param([string]$Text)
    Write-Host "[WARN] $Text" -ForegroundColor Yellow
}

function Write-Err {
    param([string]$Text)
    Write-Host "[ERROR] $Text" -ForegroundColor Red
}

Clear-Host
Write-Host "==========================================================" -ForegroundColor Magenta
Write-Host "   MiKTeX & LuaLaTeX One-Click Windows Automated Setup    " -ForegroundColor White
Write-Host "==========================================================" -ForegroundColor Magenta
Write-Host "Target: Full LaTeX compiler suite with on-the-fly packages" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
Write-Host "Designed for: Antigravity IDE, VS Code, and CLI environments`n" -ForegroundColor DarkGray

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Check Existing Installation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Write-Step "Checking environment for existing LaTeX installations..."

$ExistingLua = Get-Command lualatex.exe -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
$ExistingPdf = Get-Command pdflatex.exe -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

if ($ExistingLua -and $ExistingPdf) {
    Write-Success "Found existing LaTeX installation on PATH:"
    Write-Info "  LuaLaTeX: $($ExistingLua.Source)"
    Write-Info "  pdfLaTeX: $($ExistingPdf.Source)"
    
    $reinstall = $false
    if (-not $NonInteractive) {
        $choice = Read-Host "`nLaTeX is already installed. Do you want to re-run configuration / repair? (y/N)"
        if ($choice -match '^[Yy]') { $reinstall = $true }
    }
    
    if (-not $reinstall) {
        Write-Host "`nSkipping installation. Proceeding to verification and configuration..." -ForegroundColor Green
        & (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "verify.ps1") -SkipPause
        if (-not $NonInteractive) {
            Write-Host "`nPress any key to exit..." -ForegroundColor Gray
            [Console]::ReadKey($true) | Out-Null
        }
        return
    }
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Determine Installer Strategy
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$WingetAvailable = $false
$WingetCmd = Get-Command winget.exe -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

if ($WingetCmd -and ($Method -ne "DirectDownload")) {
    try {
        $testWinget = & winget.exe --version 2>&1
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {
            $WingetAvailable = $true
            Write-Info "Windows Package Manager (winget $testWinget) detected."
        }
    } catch {
        Write-Warn "winget execution failed. Falling back to direct download."
    }
}

$InstallSuccess = $false

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Strategy A: WinGet Installation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if ($WingetAvailable -and ($Method -eq "Auto" -or $Method -eq "Winget")) {
    Write-Step "Attempting installation via Windows Package Manager (winget)..."
    Write-Info "Executing: winget install --id MiKTeX.MiKTeX -e --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements"
    
    try {
        $proc = Start-Process -FilePath "winget.exe" `
            -ArgumentList "install --id MiKTeX.MiKTeX -e --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements" `
            -NoNewWindow -PassThru -Wait
        
        if ($proc.ExitCode -eq 0 -or $proc.ExitCode -eq 2316632065) {
            # 2316632065 is commonly returned when package is already installed
            Write-Success "winget reported successful installation."
            $InstallSuccess = $true
        } else {
            Write-Warn "winget exited with code $($proc.ExitCode). Falling back to direct installer download..."
        }
    } catch {
        Write-Warn "winget encountered an exception: $($_.Exception.Message)"
    }
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Strategy B: Direct CTAN Installer Download & Silent Execution
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if (-not $InstallSuccess) {
    Write-Step "Downloading official Basic MiKTeX Windows 64-bit installer..."
    
    $DownloadUrl = "https://miktex.org/download/ctan/systems/win32/miktex/setup/windows-x64/basic-miktex-25.12-x64.exe"
    $TempInstaller = Join-Path $env:TEMP "basic-miktex-setup-x64.exe"
    
    Write-Info "Source: $DownloadUrl"
    Write-Info "Target: $TempInstaller"
    
    if (Test-Path $TempInstaller) {
        Remove-Item $TempInstaller -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    }
    
    try {
        [Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = [Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls12 -bor [Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls13
        $webClient = New-Object System.Net.WebClient
        
        $lastReported = 0
        $progressEvent = Register-ObjectEvent -InputObject $webClient -EventName DownloadProgressChanged -Action {
            param($sender, $e)
            $percent = $e.ProgressPercentage
            if ($percent -ge ($script:lastReported + 10)) {
                $script:lastReported = $percent
                Write-Progress -Activity "Downloading Basic MiKTeX Installer" `
                    -Status "$percent% complete ($([math]::Round($e.BytesReceived/1MB, 1)) MB / $([math]::Round($e.TotalBytesToReceive/1MB, 1)) MB)" `
                    -PercentComplete $percent
            }
        }
        
        $webClient.DownloadFile($DownloadUrl, $TempInstaller)
        Unregister-Event -SourceIdentifier $progressEvent.Name -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        Write-Progress -Activity "Downloading Basic MiKTeX Installer" -Completed
        
        Write-Success "Installer downloaded successfully ($([math]::Round((Get-Item $TempInstaller).Length / 1MB, 2)) MB)."
    } catch {
        Write-Err "Failed to download installer via WebClient. Retrying with curl.exe..."
        $curlCmd = Get-Command curl.exe -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        if ($curlCmd) {
            & curl.exe -L --retry 3 -o $TempInstaller $DownloadUrl
            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or -not (Test-Path $TempInstaller)) {
                throw "curl.exe failed to download MiKTeX from $DownloadUrl"
            }
            Write-Success "curl download complete."
        } else {
            throw "Failed to download installer: $($_.Exception.Message)"
        }
    }
    
    Write-Step "Running unattended installation..."
    Write-Info "Options: --unattended --auto-install=yes --paper-size=A4"
    Write-Info "Please wait 1-3 minutes while binaries are extracted and configured..."
    
    $installArgs = @(
        "--unattended",
        "--auto-install=yes",
        "--paper-size=A4"
    )
    
    $proc = Start-Process -FilePath $TempInstaller -ArgumentList $installArgs -Wait -PassThru
    if ($proc.ExitCode -ne 0) {
        Write-Warn "Installer exited with code $($proc.ExitCode). Verifying disk contents..."
    } else {
        Write-Success "Installer process completed successfully."
    }
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Locate MiKTeX Binaries & Update Environment PATH
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Write-Step "Locating MiKTeX binaries and updating system PATH..."

$PossibleBinPaths = @(
    (Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA "Programs\MiKTeX\miktex\bin\x64"),
    (Join-Path $env:ProgramFiles "MiKTeX\miktex\bin\x64"),
    (Join-Path ${env:ProgramFiles(x86)} "MiKTeX\miktex\bin\x64")
)

$FoundBinPath = $null
foreach ($path in $PossibleBinPaths) {
    if (Test-Path (Join-Path $path "lualatex.exe")) {
        $FoundBinPath = $path
        break
    }
}

if (-not $FoundBinPath) {
    # Recursive fallback search
    $searchRoots = @((Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA "Programs\MiKTeX"), (Join-Path $env:ProgramFiles "MiKTeX"))
    foreach ($root in $searchRoots) {
        if (Test-Path $root) {
            $matched = Get-ChildItem -Path $root -Filter "lualatex.exe" -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 1
            if ($matched) {
                $FoundBinPath = $matched.DirectoryName
                break
            }
        }
    }
}

if (-not $FoundBinPath) {
    Write-Err "Could not automatically locate 'lualatex.exe' after installation."
    Write-Info "Please check if your antivirus blocked the installer or manually check C:\Program Files\MiKTeX or AppData."
    throw "Binary search failure."
}

Write-Success "Discovered MiKTeX binaries at: $FoundBinPath"

# Refresh current process PATH
if ($env:PATH -notmatch [regex]::Escape($FoundBinPath)) {
    $env:PATH = "$FoundBinPath;$env:PATH"
    Write-Info "Added to current session PATH."
}

# Persist to User Environment PATH
$UserPath = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("PATH", [EnvironmentVariableTarget]::User)
if ($UserPath -notmatch [regex]::Escape($FoundBinPath)) {
    $NewUserPath = "$FoundBinPath;$UserPath"
    [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("PATH", $NewUserPath, [EnvironmentVariableTarget]::User)
    Write-Success "Persisted '$FoundBinPath' to User Environment PATH."
} else {
    Write-Info "Path is already present in User Environment variables."
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Configure On-The-Fly Package Installation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Write-Step "Configuring automatic on-the-fly package installation..."

$InitExMf = Join-Path $FoundBinPath "initexmf.exe"
if (Test-Path $InitExMf) {
    try {
        & $InitExMf --set-config-value "[MPM]AutoInstall=1" | Out-Null
        Write-Success "Package Manager Auto-Install enabled ([MPM]AutoInstall=1)."
        
        Write-Info "Updating filename database (fndb)..."
        & $InitExMf --update-fndb | Out-Null
        Write-Success "Filename database updated."
    } catch {
        Write-Warn "Could not update initexmf configuration: $($_.Exception.Message)"
    }
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Verification Tests
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Write-Step "Running sanity checks on installed engines..."

$TestLua = & (Join-Path $FoundBinPath "lualatex.exe") --version 2>&1 | Select-Object -First 1
$TestPdf = & (Join-Path $FoundBinPath "pdflatex.exe") --version 2>&1 | Select-Object -First 1

if ($TestLua) {
    Write-Success "LuaLaTeX verification: $TestLua"
} else {
    Write-Err "Failed to execute lualatex.exe"
}

if ($TestPdf) {
    Write-Success "pdfLaTeX verification: $TestPdf"
} else {
    Write-Err "Failed to execute pdflatex.exe"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Check Integration with realtime-tex (rtex)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Write-Step "Checking integration with Realtime TeX (rtex)..."

$PossibleRtexPaths = @(
    (Join-Path $env:APPDATA "Antigravity IDE\User\globalStorage\henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex\rtex-release\v0.0.7\bin\rtex.exe"),
    (Join-Path $env:APPDATA "Code\User\globalStorage\henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex\rtex-release\v0.0.7\bin\rtex.exe")
)

$RtexFound = $null
foreach ($p in $PossibleRtexPaths) {
    if (Test-Path $p) {
        $RtexFound = $p
        break
    }
}

if ($RtexFound) {
    Write-Info "Found rtex at: $RtexFound"
    Write-Info "Running 'rtex doctor'..."
    try {
        $doctorOutput = & $RtexFound doctor 2>&1
        $doctorOutput | ForEach-Object { Write-Host "   $_" -ForegroundColor DarkGray }
        if ($doctorOutput -match 'lualatex:\s+ok|LuaLaTeX found|rtex \d') {
            Write-Success "rtex successfully recognized LuaLaTeX!"
        }
    } catch {
        Write-Warn "rtex doctor check was inconclusive."
    }
} else {
    Write-Info "No VS Code / Antigravity IDE realtime-tex storage found. (Extension can be installed anytime)."
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Summary & Completion
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Write-Host "`n==========================================================" -ForegroundColor Green
Write-Host "   INSTALLATION & CONFIGURATION COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!   " -ForegroundColor White
Write-Host "==========================================================" -ForegroundColor Green
Write-Host "Summary of Setup:" -ForegroundColor White
Write-Host "  1. MiKTeX suite installed at: $FoundBinPath"
Write-Host "  2. System User PATH updated (restart open terminals / IDE to refresh)."
Write-Host "  3. Automatic package download enabled (no manual CTAN package installs needed)."
Write-Host "  4. LuaLaTeX and pdfLaTeX are operational."
Write-Host "  5. Live preview in Realtime TeX / LaTeX Workshop is now ready to use.`n"

if (-not $NonInteractive) {
    Write-Host "Press any key to exit..." -ForegroundColor Gray
    [Console]::ReadKey($true) | Out-Null
}

<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Verification & Health Check Script for MiKTeX, LuaLaTeX, and Editor Bridges.
.DESCRIPTION
    Checks whether LaTeX binaries are on PATH, tests LuaLaTeX compilation on
    a minimal test document, verifies on-the-fly package fetching, and inspects
    rtex (Realtime TeX) integration.
.PARAMETER SkipPause
    Skips the interactive "Press any key to exit" pause.
#>

[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [switch]$SkipPause
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Continue"

function Write-Check {
    param([string]$Title, [bool]$Passed, [string]$Details = "")
    if ($Passed) {
        Write-Host " [PASS] " -ForegroundColor Green -NoNewline
        Write-Host "$Title" -ForegroundColor White -NoNewline
        if ($Details) { Write-Host " ($Details)" -ForegroundColor Gray } else { Write-Host "" }
    } else {
        Write-Host " [FAIL] " -ForegroundColor Red -NoNewline
        Write-Host "$Title" -ForegroundColor Yellow -NoNewline
        if ($Details) { Write-Host " - $Details" -ForegroundColor DarkYellow } else { Write-Host "" }
    }
}

Clear-Host
Write-Host "==========================================================" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "      MiKTeX & LuaLaTeX Environment Diagnostic Check       " -ForegroundColor White
Write-Host "==========================================================" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host ""

# 1. Binary availability
$luaCmd = Get-Command lualatex.exe -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
$pdfCmd = Get-Command pdflatex.exe -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
$xeCmd  = Get-Command xelatex.exe  -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
$initCmd = Get-Command initexmf.exe -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

Write-Check "LuaLaTeX Binary" ($null -ne $luaCmd) $(if ($luaCmd) { $luaCmd.Source } else { "Not found on PATH" })
Write-Check "pdfLaTeX Binary" ($null -ne $pdfCmd) $(if ($pdfCmd) { $pdfCmd.Source } else { "Not found on PATH" })
Write-Check "XeLaTeX Binary"  ($null -ne $xeCmd)  $(if ($xeCmd)  { $xeCmd.Source }  else { "Not found on PATH" })
Write-Check "MiKTeX Maintenance Utility (initexmf)" ($null -ne $initCmd) $(if ($initCmd) { $initCmd.Source } else { "Not found on PATH" })

# 2. Check Package Auto-Install Configuration
if ($initCmd) {
    try {
        $val = & $initCmd.Source --show-config-value "[MPM]AutoInstall" 2>&1
        $isAuto = ($val -match "1|yes")
        Write-Check "On-the-fly package download enabled" $isAuto "Value: $val"
    } catch {
        Write-Check "On-the-fly package download check" $false "Failed to query initexmf"
    }
}

# 3. Test LuaLaTeX End-to-End Compilation
Write-Host "`n--> Testing LuaLaTeX Document Compilation..." -ForegroundColor Cyan

$testDir = Join-Path $env:TEMP "miktex_verify_test"
if (Test-Path $testDir) { Remove-Item $testDir -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $testDir | Out-Null

$testTex = Join-Path $testDir "test.tex"
@"

\usepackage{amsmath}
\begin{document}
Hello from LuaLaTeX!
Equation: $E = mc^2$
\end{document}
"@ | Out-File -FilePath $testTex -Encoding ascii

$compileSuccess = $false
if ($luaCmd) {
    Push-Location $testDir
    try {
        $output = & $luaCmd.Source --interaction=nonstopmode test.tex 2>&1
        $pdfOut = Join-Path $testDir "test.pdf"
        if (Test-Path $pdfOut) {
            $compileSuccess = $true
        }
    } finally {
        Pop-Location
    }
}

Write-Check "LuaLaTeX Sample Compilation (test.tex -> test.pdf)" $compileSuccess $(if ($compileSuccess) { "PDF generated successfully" } else { "Compilation failed or binary missing" })

# Clean up test files
Remove-Item $testDir -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

# 4. Check Realtime TeX (rtex) Doctor
Write-Host "`n--> Testing Realtime TeX (rtex) Engine..." -ForegroundColor Cyan
$PossibleRtexPaths = @(
    (Join-Path $env:APPDATA "Antigravity IDE\User\globalStorage\henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex\rtex-release\v0.0.7\bin\rtex.exe"),
    (Join-Path $env:APPDATA "Code\User\globalStorage\henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex\rtex-release\v0.0.7\bin\rtex.exe")
)

$rtexBin = $PossibleRtexPaths | Where-Object { Test-Path $_ } | Select-Object -First 1

if ($rtexBin) {
    try {
        $doc = & $rtexBin doctor 2>&1
        $rtexPassed = ($doc -match "lualatex:\s+ok" -or -not ($doc -match "missing"))
        Write-Check "rtex doctor status" $rtexPassed "Engine at: $rtexBin"
        if (-not $rtexPassed) {

}

Write-Host "==========================================================`n" -ForegroundColor Cyan

if (-not $SkipPause) {
    Write-Host "Press any key to exit..." -ForegroundColor Gray

}

# Windows MiKTeX & LuaLaTeX One-Click Automated Setup

[![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/Platform-Windows%2010%20%7C%2011%20(x64)-blue.svg)](#)
[![PowerShell](https://img.shields.io/badge/PowerShell-5.1%20%7C%207+-darkblue.svg)](#)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Engine](https://img.shields.io/badge/LaTeX-LuaLaTeX%20%7C%20pdfLaTeX%20%7C%20XeLaTeX-purple.svg)](#)

A zero-touch, automated one-click installer and environment configurator for **MiKTeX**, **LuaLaTeX**, and **pdfLaTeX** on Windows. 

Designed specifically to bootstrap LaTeX rendering for **Antigravity IDE**, **Visual Studio Code** (including [Realtime TeX (`henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex`)](https://github.com/HenryXiaoYang/realtime-tex) and [LaTeX Workshop (`James-Yu.latex-workshop`)](https://github.com/James-Yu/LaTeX-Workshop)), and standalone command-line LaTeX authoring.

---

## Table of Contents
- [The Problem Solved](#the-problem-solved)
- [Key Features](#key-features)
- [Directory Structure](#directory-structure)
- [Quick Start](#quick-start)
- [CLI Usage & Parameters](#cli-usage--parameters)
- [Environment Verification](#environment-verification)
- [How It Works Under the Hood](#how-it-works-under-the-hood)
- [Troubleshooting & FAQ](#troubleshooting--faq)
- [License](#license)

---

## The Problem Solved

Modern VS Code extensions such as **Realtime TeX (`rtex`)** provide sub-millisecond, incremental LaTeX previewing as you type, but they depend on an unmodified system `lualatex` binary. When developers open LaTeX files without a pre-installed TeX distribution, they encounter the classic blocker:

```text
Error: lualatex not found on PATH (source build/texlive.env or set RTEX_TEXLIVE_BIN)
Caused by:
    lualatex not found
```

Manual installation often requires navigating installer wizards, configuring environment variables, and dealing with missing package errors when compiling documents that use `amsmath`, `listings`, or `IEEEtran`.

This repository provides an automated, idempotent one-click installer that sets up MiKTeX silently, enables automatic on-the-fly package fetching, updates your environment variables, and verifies that `rtex` and your editors detect the engine immediately.

---

## Key Features

- **One-Click Execution**: Simply double-click `install.bat` from File Explorer—no manual prompts required.
- **Dual Installation Strategy**:
  1. **Primary**: Fast installation using Windows Package Manager (`winget`).
  2. **Automated Fallback**: Direct high-speed download of the official Basic MiKTeX installer from CTAN mirrors with resume logic if `winget` is unavailable or restricted.
- **On-the-Fly Package Installation Preconfigured**: Enables `[MPM]AutoInstall=1` and refreshes the filename database (`fndb`), meaning any missing CTAN package (`IEEEtran`, `listings`, `booktabs`, `xcolor`, etc.) is downloaded automatically during compilation without popup dialogs.
- **Persistent User PATH Injection**: Detects the installation directory (`AppData\Local\Programs\MiKTeX\miktex\bin\x64` or `Program Files\MiKTeX\miktex\bin\x64`), updates the active session, and injects it permanently into the Windows User Environment variables.
- **Realtime TeX (`rtex`) & IDE Detection**: Automatically checks for local `rtex` daemon storage in Antigravity IDE and VS Code, executing `rtex doctor` to ensure the live editor preview works immediately.
- **Comprehensive Diagnostic Suite**: Includes `verify.bat` and `verify.ps1` with an automated end-to-end sample compilation check.

---

## Directory Structure

```text
windows-miktex-installer/
├── install.bat          # Double-clickable Windows Explorer launcher
├── install.ps1          # Robust PowerShell automation script
├── verify.bat           # Quick verification launcher
├── verify.ps1           # Environment diagnostic and sample compiler test
├── test/
│   └── sample.tex       # Multi-package test document (amsmath, listings, booktabs)
├── .gitignore           # Git ignore rules for TeX build artifacts and installers
├── LICENSE              # MIT License
└── README.md            # Repository documentation
```

---

## Quick Start

### Option A: Double-Click (GUI)
1. Navigate into the `windows-miktex-installer` folder.
2. Double-click **`install.bat`**.
3. Allow the installer to complete (typically 1–3 minutes).
4. Restart your editor or open terminal windows so the updated `PATH` is loaded.

### Option B: PowerShell Terminal
```powershell
# Run from repository root
cd windows-miktex-installer
.\install.ps1
```

For automated CI/CD or non-interactive setups:
```powershell
.\install.ps1 -NonInteractive
```

---

## CLI Usage & Parameters

`install.ps1` supports flexible parameters:

```powershell
.\install.ps1 [-Method <Auto | Winget | DirectDownload>] [-NonInteractive]
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-Method` | String | `Auto` | Selects installation backend: `Auto` (tries `winget` then CTAN fallback), `Winget` (winget only), or `DirectDownload` (downloads basic-miktex installer directly from CTAN). |
| `-NonInteractive` | Switch | `False` | Suppresses interactive pauses ("Press any key to exit"), ideal for scripts and batch jobs. |

---

## Environment Verification

To verify that your installation is healthy at any time:

```powershell
.\verify.ps1
```
Or double-click **`verify.bat`**.

**Expected Diagnostic Output:**
```text
==========================================================
      MiKTeX & LuaLaTeX Environment Diagnostic Check       
==========================================================

 [PASS] LuaLaTeX Binary (C:\Users\...\AppData\Local\Programs\MiKTeX\miktex\bin\x64\lualatex.exe)
 [PASS] pdfLaTeX Binary (C:\Users\...\AppData\Local\Programs\MiKTeX\miktex\bin\x64\pdflatex.exe)
 [PASS] XeLaTeX Binary (C:\Users\...\AppData\Local\Programs\MiKTeX\miktex\bin\x64\xelatex.exe)
 [PASS] MiKTeX Maintenance Utility (initexmf) (C:\...\initexmf.exe)
 [PASS] On-the-fly package download enabled (Value: 1)

--> Testing LuaLaTeX Document Compilation...
 [PASS] LuaLaTeX Sample Compilation (test.tex -> test.pdf) (PDF generated successfully)

--> Testing Realtime TeX (rtex) Engine...
 [PASS] rtex doctor status (Engine at: C:\Users\...\rtex.exe)

==========================================================
 System is ready for LaTeX authoring and real-time preview!
==========================================================
```

---

## How It Works Under the Hood

1. **Detection**: Queries `Get-Command lualatex.exe` and `pdflatex.exe` across the existing `PATH`.
2. **Installation Strategy**:
   - Tries `winget install --id MiKTeX.MiKTeX -e --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements`.
   - If `winget` is missing or fails, fetches the official 64-bit Basic MiKTeX setup executable from CTAN (`basic-miktex-*-x64.exe`) with progress reporting.
   - Executes the installer with non-interactive flags:
     ```cmd
     basic-miktex-setup-x64.exe --unattended --auto-install=yes --paper-size=A4
     ```
3. **Configuration**:
   - Queries `[EnvironmentVariableTarget]::User` and appends the binary directory to ensure future command prompts and IDE sessions find the binaries.
   - Executes `initexmf --set-config-value [MPM]AutoInstall=1` to guarantee silent, on-demand package downloading.
   - Runs `initexmf --update-fndb` to build the TeX font and filename directory indexes.
4. **Editor Validation**:
   - Inspects `%APPDATA%\Antigravity IDE` and `%APPDATA%\Code` for the `henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex` engine.
   - Runs `rtex doctor` to assert that `lualatex: ok` is returned.

---

## Troubleshooting & FAQ

#### 1. "lualatex not found" persists in VS Code after installation
Windows environment variable changes do not propagate to already-running applications. **Close and restart VS Code / Antigravity IDE** completely so it picks up the newly updated User `PATH`.

#### 2. Antivirus or Windows SmartScreen warnings
Because the script executes an installer in unattended mode, Windows Defender or third-party antivirus suites may occasionally prompt for confirmation. Select "More info" $\rightarrow$ "Run anyway" if prompted.

#### 3. Compiling an IEEEtran conference paper fails on first run
When compiling a document with new packages for the first time, MiKTeX will download the packages in the background. Ensure you have an active internet connection on the first compile. Subsequent runs use the cached packages from local disk and compile instantly.

---

## License

This project is licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

## 1. User Request Summary
1. **Initial Issue**: The user requested preparing LaTeX rendering in the workspace to edit and preview the project final report located at [`Project.MM/FinalReport/`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/Project.MM/FinalReport). When previewing with the extension `henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex`, the live preview crashed with:
   ```text
   Error: lualatex not found on PATH (source build/texlive.env or set RTEX_TEXLIVE_BIN)
   Caused by:
       lualatex not found
   ```
2. **Follow-Up Request**: Implement and create a one-click install script for **Option 2 (MiKTeX & LuaLaTeX automated system installation)** at the project root in a dedicated new folder designed to serve as a standalone GitHub repository.

---

## 2. Inspected Artifacts & Environment Diagnostics
1. **Target Report Directory**:
   - [`Project.MM/FinalReport/v2_MM_Lab_Final_Report(PresentationAid).tex`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/Project.MM/FinalReport/v2_MM_Lab_Final_Report(PresentationAid).tex) (complete 206-line IEEEtran conference paper report on the ESP32 micro-NAS & static web hosting node).
   - [`Project.MM/FinalReport/conference_101719.tex`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/Project.MM/FinalReport/conference_101719.tex) (IEEE conference paper template).
   - [`Project.MM/FinalReport/IEEEtran.cls`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/Project.MM/FinalReport/IEEEtran.cls) (local document class).
   - [`Project.MM/FinalReport/fig1.png`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/Project.MM/FinalReport/fig1.png) (figure graphic).
2. **IDE Extension State**:
   - `henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex-0.0.5-universal` installed in `C:\Users\gsmur\.antigravity-ide\extensions\`.
   - The compiled engine `rtex.exe` (v0.0.7) was present in global storage at `C:\Users\gsmur\AppData\Roaming\Antigravity IDE\User\globalStorage\henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex\rtex-release\v0.0.7\bin\rtex.exe`.
3. **Environment Inspection**:
   - Neither `lualatex`, `pdflatex`, `xelatex`, `texlive`, nor `miktex` existed on the system `PATH`.

---

## 3. Analysis & Key Insights (Root Cause Investigation)

### 3.1 The Architecture of `henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex` and `rtex`
`realtime-tex` (`rtex`) provides millisecond-level live LaTeX rendering by keeping a warm, persistent **LuaLaTeX** process alive in the background with the document preamble pre-loaded. When the author edits text, `rtex` does not recompile the entire document; instead, it re-typesets *only* the specific paragraph currently being edited in ~1 millisecond using LuaLaTeX callbacks.

However, **`rtex` is only an orchestration daemon and bridge**—it does not bundle the TeX compiler binaries, macro packages, or fonts itself. It strictly delegates all compilation passes to `lualatex`.

### 3.2 Verification via `rtex doctor`
Directly invoking the bundled diagnostic tool revealed the exact failure point:
```powershell
& "C:\Users\gsmur\AppData\Roaming\Antigravity IDE\User\globalStorage\henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex\rtex-release\v0.0.7\bin\rtex.exe" doctor
```
**Diagnostic Output:**
```text
rtex 0.0.7
support files: C:\Users\gsmur\AppData\Roaming\Antigravity IDE\User\globalStorage\henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex\rtex-release\v0.0.7\share\rtex\tex
lualatex: missing (lualatex not found on PATH (source build/texlive.env or set RTEX_TEXLIVE_BIN))
```

### 3.3 The Missing System Component: LuaLaTeX
Because the host machine lacks a TeX distribution (TeX Live or MiKTeX), `rtex` fails to spawn the compiler process when initiating the live preview panel.

---

## 4. Implementation: Standalone `windows-miktex-installer` Repository

To provide a permanent, reproducible, and open-source solution that the user can turn into an independent repository, a standalone suite was created under [`windows-miktex-installer/`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer).

### 4.1 Architecture & Component Design
The folder is structured as a self-contained, distribution-ready repository:
- **[`install.bat`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer/install.bat)**: Double-clickable batch launcher for Windows Explorer. Handles elevation detection and passes execution to PowerShell with `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass`.
- **[`install.ps1`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer/install.ps1)**: Core automation script featuring colored logging, idempotency checks, dual installation backends, binary path resolution, and editor integration testing.
- **[`verify.bat`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer/verify.bat)** & **[`verify.ps1`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer/verify.ps1)**: Non-destructive health check tool verifying binary detection, on-the-fly download configuration, sample LaTeX compilation, and `rtex doctor` status.
- **[`test/sample.tex`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer/test/sample.tex)**: Multi-package test document using `amsmath`, `listings`, and `booktabs` to validate automated package fetching.
- **[`README.md`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer/README.md)**: Full GitHub documentation with architecture diagrams, parameters, usage guides, and troubleshooting tips.
- **[`LICENSE`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer/LICENSE)**: Standard MIT License.
- **[`.gitignore`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer/.gitignore)**: Clean ignore rules for temporary installer executables, logs, and LaTeX auxiliary files.

### 4.2 Dual-Strategy Installation Logic (`winget` + CTAN Fallback)
The installer implements an automatic fallback mechanism:
1. **Primary Backend (`winget`)**:
   ```powershell
   winget install --id MiKTeX.MiKTeX -e --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements
   ```
2. **Fallback Backend (Direct CTAN Download)**:
   If `winget` is unavailable, corrupted, or blocked, the script downloads the official setup executable directly:
   `https://miktex.org/download/ctan/systems/win32/miktex/setup/windows-x64/basic-miktex-25.12-x64.exe`
   And executes it silently:
   ```cmd
   basic-miktex-setup-x64.exe --unattended --auto-install=yes --paper-size=A4
   ```

### 4.3 Zero-Prompt Package Configuration (`[MPM]AutoInstall=1`)
To eliminate intrusive GUI popups when LaTeX documents compile with new packages:
1. Discovers the installed binary path (`AppData\Local\Programs\MiKTeX\miktex\bin\x64` or `Program Files\MiKTeX\miktex\bin\x64`).
2. Configures the MiKTeX Package Manager:

When previewing with the extension `henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex`, the live preview crashed with:
   ```text

   Caused by:
   ```

2. **Follow-Up Request**: Implement and create a one-click install script for **Option 2 (MiKTeX & LuaLaTeX automated system installation)** at the project root in a dedicated new folder designed to serve as a standalone GitHub repository.

## 3. Analysis & Key Insights (Root Cause Investigation)

### 3.1 The Architecture of `henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex` and `rtex`
`realtime-tex` (`rtex`) provides millisecond-level live LaTeX rendering by keeping a warm, persistent **LuaLaTeX** process alive in the background with the document preamble pre-loaded. When the author edits text, `rtex` does not recompile the entire document; instead, it re-typesets *only* the specific paragraph currently being edited in ~1 millisecond using LuaLaTeX callbacks.

However, **`rtex` is only an orchestration daemon and bridge**—it does not bundle the TeX compiler binaries, macro packages, or fonts itself. It strictly delegates all compilation passes to `lualatex`.

### 3.2 Verification via `rtex doctor`
Directly invoking the bundled diagnostic tool revealed the exact failure point:
```powershell
& "C:\Users\gsmur\AppData\Roaming\Antigravity IDE\User\globalStorage\henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex\rtex-release\v0.0.7\bin\rtex.exe" doctor
```

```text
lualatex: missing (lualatex not found on PATH (source build/texlive.env or set RTEX_TEXLIVE_BIN))
```

### 3.3 The Missing System Component: LuaLaTeX
Because the host machine lacks a TeX distribution (TeX Live or MiKTeX), `rtex` fails to spawn the compiler process when initiating the live preview panel.

## 4. Implementation: Standalone `windows-miktex-installer` Repository

To provide a permanent, reproducible, and open-source solution that the user can turn into an independent repository, a standalone suite was created under [`windows-miktex-installer/`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer).

### 4.1 Architecture & Component Design
The folder is structured as a self-contained, distribution-ready repository:
- **[`install.bat`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer/install.bat)**: Double-clickable batch launcher for Windows Explorer. Handles elevation detection and passes execution to PowerShell with `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass`.
- **[`install.ps1`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer/install.ps1)**: Core automation script featuring colored logging, idempotency checks, dual installation backends, binary path resolution, and editor integration testing.
- **[`verify.bat`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer/verify.bat)** & **[`verify.ps1`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer/verify.ps1)**: Non-destructive health check tool verifying binary detection, on-the-fly download configuration, sample LaTeX compilation, and `rtex doctor` status.
- **[`test/sample.tex`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer/test/sample.tex)**: Multi-package test document using `amsmath`, `listings`, and `booktabs` to validate automated package fetching.
- **[`README.md`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer/README.md)**: Full GitHub documentation with architecture diagrams, parameters, usage guides, and troubleshooting tips.
- **[`LICENSE`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer/LICENSE)**: Standard MIT License.
- **[`.gitignore`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer/.gitignore)**: Clean ignore rules for temporary installer executables, logs, and LaTeX auxiliary files.

### 4.2 Dual-Strategy Installation Logic (`winget` + CTAN Fallback)
The installer implements an automatic fallback mechanism:
1. **Primary Backend (`winget`)**:
   ```powershell
   winget install --id MiKTeX.MiKTeX -e --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements
   ```
2. **Fallback Backend (Direct CTAN Download)**:
   If `winget` is unavailable, corrupted, or blocked, the script downloads the official setup executable directly:
   `https://miktex.org/download/ctan/systems/win32/miktex/setup/windows-x64/basic-miktex-25.12-x64.exe`
   And executes it silently:
   ```cmd
   basic-miktex-setup-x64.exe --unattended --auto-install=yes --paper-size=A4
   ```

### 4.3 Zero-Prompt Package Configuration (`[MPM]AutoInstall=1`)
To eliminate intrusive GUI popups when LaTeX documents compile with new packages:
1. Discovers the installed binary path (`AppData\Local\Programs\MiKTeX\miktex\bin\x64` or `Program Files\MiKTeX\miktex\bin\x64`).
2. Configures the MiKTeX Package Manager:
   ```cmd
   initexmf.exe --set-config-value [MPM]AutoInstall=1
   initexmf.exe --update-fndb
   ```
3. Injects the binary directory into the current process `$env:PATH` and permanently persists it to `[EnvironmentVariableTarget]::User`.

## 3. Analysis & Key Insights (Root Cause Investigation)

### 3.1 The Architecture of `henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex` and `rtex`
`realtime-tex` (`rtex`) provides millisecond-level live LaTeX rendering by keeping a warm, persistent **LuaLaTeX** process alive in the background with the document preamble pre-loaded. When the author edits text, `rtex` does not recompile the entire document; instead, it re-typesets *only* the specific paragraph currently being edited in ~1 millisecond using LuaLaTeX callbacks.

However, **`rtex` is only an orchestration daemon and bridge**—it does not bundle the TeX compiler binaries, macro packages, or fonts itself. It strictly delegates all compilation passes to `lualatex`.

### 3.2 Verification via `rtex doctor`
Directly invoking the bundled diagnostic tool revealed the exact failure point:
```powershell
& "C:\Users\gsmur\AppData\Roaming\Antigravity IDE\User\globalStorage\henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex\rtex-release\v0.0.7\bin\rtex.exe" doctor
```

```text
lualatex: missing (lualatex not found on PATH (source build/texlive.env or set RTEX_TEXLIVE_BIN))
```

### 3.3 The Missing System Component: LuaLaTeX
Because the host machine lacked a TeX distribution (TeX Live or MiKTeX), `rtex` fails to spawn the compiler process when initiating the live preview panel.

## 4. Implementation: Standalone `windows-miktex-installer` Repository

A self-contained repository was created under [`windows-miktex-installer/`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer).

### 4.1 Architecture & Component Design
- **[`install.bat`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer/install.bat)**: Double-clickable batch launcher for Windows Explorer. Handles elevation detection and passes execution to PowerShell with `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass`.
- **[`install.ps1`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer/install.ps1)**: Core automation script featuring colored logging, idempotency checks, dual installation backends, binary path resolution, and editor integration testing.
- **[`verify.bat`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer/verify.bat)** & **[`verify.ps1`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer/verify.ps1)**: Non-destructive health check tool verifying binary detection, on-the-fly download configuration, sample LaTeX compilation, and `rtex doctor` status.
- **[`test/sample.tex`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer/test/sample.tex)**: Multi-package test document using `amsmath`, `listings`, and `booktabs` to validate automated package fetching.
- **[`README.md`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer/README.md)**: Full GitHub documentation with architecture diagrams, parameters, usage guides, and troubleshooting tips.
- **[`LICENSE`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer/LICENSE)**: Standard MIT License.
- **[`.gitignore`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer/.gitignore)**: Clean ignore rules for temporary installer executables, logs, and LaTeX auxiliary files.

### 4.2 Dual-Strategy Installation Logic (`winget` + CTAN Fallback)
The installer implements an automatic fallback mechanism:
1. **Primary Backend (`winget`)**:
   ```powershell
   winget install --id MiKTeX.MiKTeX -e --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements
   ```
2. **Fallback Backend (Direct CTAN Download)**:
   If `winget` is unavailable or restricted, the script downloads:
   `https://miktex.org/download/ctan/systems/win32/miktex/setup/windows-x64/basic-miktex-25.12-x64.exe`
   And executes it silently:
   ```cmd
   basic-miktex-setup-x64.exe --unattended --auto-install=yes --paper-size=A4
   ```

### 4.3 Zero-Prompt Package Configuration (`[MPM]AutoInstall=1`)
To eliminate intrusive GUI popups during compilation:
1. Discovers the installed binary path (`C:\Users\gsmur\AppData\Local\Programs\MiKTeX\miktex\bin\x64`).
2. Configures the MiKTeX Package Manager:
   ```cmd
   initexmf.exe --set-config-value [MPM]AutoInstall=1
   initexmf.exe --update-fndb
   ```
3. Injects the binary directory into the current process `$env:PATH` and permanently persists it to `[EnvironmentVariableTarget]::User`.

## 5. Troubleshooting: Launcher Premature Exit & Stale Process PATH

When the user executed `install.bat` and `verify.bat`, four distinct Windows runtime nuances caused the perceived failure:

### 5.1 The Window Closing Issue in `install.bat`
In the initial version of `install.bat`, the batch script only paused if `%errorlevel%` was non-zero. When the script completed with code `0`, cmd.exe immediately hit `exit /b 0`, instantly terminating the console window before the user could read the output.
**Resolution**: Added a mandatory `pause` before exiting on both success and failure paths.

### 5.2 CMD Title Command Splitting (`&` character)
The header `title MiKTeX & LuaLaTeX Verification Tool` contained an unquoted ampersand (`&`). In standard Windows `cmd.exe`, `&` acts as an unconditional command separator. Consequently, Windows executed `title MiKTeX` and immediately attempted to execute `LuaLaTeX` as a shell command, printing `'LuaLaTeX' is not recognized as an internal or external command`.
**Resolution**: Replaced `&` with `and` in window titles (`title MiKTeX and LuaLaTeX One-Click Windows Installer`).

### 5.3 Process Environment Inheritance & Stale PATH Resolution
Windows child processes inherit environment variables from their parent process at creation time. Because open terminal sessions, File Explorer, and IDE windows were launched *before* MiKTeX wrote to the registry, their process-level `$env:PATH` remained stale. Even though MiKTeX was successfully installed at `C:\Users\gsmur\AppData\Local\Programs\MiKTeX\miktex\bin\x64`, `verify.ps1` called `Get-Command lualatex.exe`, which failed to search beyond the process's inherited `PATH`.
**Resolution**: Updated [`verify.ps1`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer/verify.ps1) to dynamically read and merge `[System.Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("PATH", "User")`, `Machine`, and known candidate installation roots at script startup.

### 5.4 Interactive vs. Redirected Console Stdin Handling
Calling `[Console]::ReadKey($true)` crashes with an `InvalidOperationException` when a script is executed from non-interactive shells or redirected pipes.
**Resolution**: Wrapped keypress prompts in `try { ... } catch {}` with `[Environment]::UserInteractive` guards.

## 3. Analysis & Key Insights (Root Cause Investigation)

### 3.1 The Architecture of `henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex` and `rtex`
`realtime-tex` (`rtex`) provides millisecond-level live LaTeX rendering by keeping a warm, persistent **LuaLaTeX** process alive in the background with the document preamble pre-loaded. When the author edits text, `rtex` does not recompile the entire document; instead, it re-typesets *only* the specific paragraph currently being edited in ~1 millisecond using LuaLaTeX callbacks.

However, **`rtex` is only an orchestration daemon and bridge**—it does not bundle the TeX compiler binaries, macro packages, or fonts itself. It strictly delegates all compilation passes to `lualatex`.

### 3.2 Verification via `rtex doctor`
Directly invoking the bundled diagnostic tool revealed the exact failure point:
```powershell
& "C:\Users\gsmur\AppData\Roaming\Antigravity IDE\User\globalStorage\henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex\rtex-release\v0.0.7\bin\rtex.exe" doctor
```
**Diagnostic Output:**
```text
rtex 0.0.7
support files: C:\Users\gsmur\AppData\Roaming\Antigravity IDE\User\globalStorage\henryxiaoyang.realtime-tex\rtex-release\v0.0.7\share\rtex\tex
lualatex: missing (lualatex not found on PATH (source build/texlive.env or set RTEX_TEXLIVE_BIN))
```

### 3.3 The Missing System Component: LuaLaTeX
Because the host machine lacked a TeX distribution (TeX Live or MiKTeX), `rtex` failed to spawn the compiler process when initiating the live preview panel.

A self-contained repository was created under [`windows-miktex-installer/`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer).

### 4.2 Dual-Strategy Installation Logic (`winget` + CTAN Fallback)
The installer implements an automatic fallback mechanism:
1. **Primary Backend (`winget`)**:
   ```powershell
   winget install --id MiKTeX.MiKTeX -e --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements
   ```
2. **Fallback Backend (Direct CTAN Download)**:
   If `winget` is unavailable or restricted, the script downloads:
   `https://miktex.org/download/ctan/systems/win32/miktex/setup/windows-x64/basic-miktex-25.12-x64.exe`
   And executes it silently:
   ```cmd
   basic-miktex-setup-x64.exe --unattended --auto-install=yes --paper-size=A4
   ```

### 4.3 Zero-Prompt Package Configuration (`[MPM]AutoInstall=1`)
To eliminate intrusive GUI popups during compilation:
1. Discovers the installed binary path (`C:\Users\gsmur\AppData\Local\Programs\MiKTeX\miktex\bin\x64`).
2. Configures the MiKTeX Package Manager:
   ```cmd
   initexmf.exe --set-config-value [MPM]AutoInstall=1
   initexmf.exe --update-fndb
   ```
3. Injects the binary directory into the current process `$env:PATH` and permanently persists it to `[EnvironmentVariableTarget]::User`.

## 5. Troubleshooting: Launcher Premature Exit & Stale Process PATH

### 5.1 The Window Closing Issue in `install.bat`
`install.bat` originally lacked a trailing pause on successful exit code `0`, causing File Explorer to instantly close the window upon completion. Added a mandatory `pause`.

### 5.2 CMD Title Command Splitting (`&` character)
`title MiKTeX & LuaLaTeX...` caused cmd.exe to treat `&` as a command separator, throwing `'LuaLaTeX' is not recognized`. Replaced with `title MiKTeX and LuaLaTeX...`.

### 5.3 Process Environment Inheritance & Stale PATH Resolution
Windows processes inherit environment variables at creation time. Existing terminal windows retain their pre-installation `PATH`. `verify.ps1` was enhanced to dynamically read `User` and `Machine` PATH from the Windows registry.

### 5.4 Interactive vs. Redirected Console Stdin Handling
`[Console]::ReadKey($true)` was guarded with `try { ... } catch {}` to prevent `InvalidOperationException` in non-interactive pipes.

## 6. Resolving Editor Process Environment Stagnation (`realtimeTex.texliveBin`)

### 6.1 The Active IDE Environment Gap
Because Antigravity IDE was open while MiKTeX was installed, its internal Node.js extension host process retained the original, pre-installation `process.env.PATH`. Therefore, pressing `Ctrl + Alt + V` spawned `rtex.exe` with the old PATH, causing `lualatex not found`.

### 6.2 Explicit Configuration Injection
Rather than requiring a full system reboot or IDE restart, the extension explicitly supports overriding the binary search via the setting:
`"realtimeTex.texliveBin": "C:\\Users\\gsmur\\AppData\\Local\\Programs\\MiKTeX\\miktex\\bin\\x64"`

This was configured directly in:
1. **User Settings**: `C:\Users\gsmur\AppData\Roaming\Antigravity IDE\User\settings.json`
2. **Workspace Settings**: [`.vscode/settings.json`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/.vscode/settings.json)

### 6.3 Installer Automation Enhancement
[`windows-miktex-installer/install.ps1`](https://github.com/b1tranger/Microprocessor_Assembly_Lab/blob/main/windows-miktex-installer/install.ps1) was enhanced to automatically inject `realtimeTex.texliveBin` into both `%APPDATA%\Antigravity IDE\User\settings.json` and `%APPDATA%\Code\User\settings.json` upon installation completion.
